selection_rationale: M10 is the active survivor after the six-hour rounds and final tail sprint. Its exact integer-time Fejer bridge removes the block-merger and continuous-reconstruction losses, including the width-one prime. Baker--Harman--Pintz now gives polynomial zero bands for both required dilations, but closure still requires one weighted joint CRT tail theorem across the remaining subexponential range. M05 remains mathematically surviving because it proves the symmetric density-scale theorem and a 6^q one-block orthant successor, but its A-line allocation is stopped: no multiscale merger was obtained and the standard continuous full-system majorant is impossible when k+1 is prime. M08 remains dormant. None is promoted; the public exponent is unchanged.
